item_description: The largest animal known to have lived on Earth, a baleen whale that filters small prey from seawater.
item_facts: Blue whales feed mainly on krill.
They produce some of the loudest sounds made by animals.
Their heart and blood vessels support circulation through an exceptionally large body.
needs_review: Size superlative, diet and physiology claims not externally verified.

item_description: A powerful, fast-swimming tuna prized as food and capable of maintaining parts of its body warmer than surrounding water.
item_facts: Several species are called bluefin tuna, including Atlantic, Pacific and southern bluefin.
They are highly migratory predators that feed on fish and squid.
Their populations have been affected by fishing pressure, with conservation status varying by species.
needs_review: Common name covers multiple species; taxonomy, behavior and conservation status need species-level review.

item_description: An intelligent, social toothed whale found in coastal and offshore waters around the world.
item_facts: Bottlenose dolphins use echolocation to find prey and navigate.
They live in social groups whose composition can change over time.
The common name includes more than one recognized species.
needs_review: Behavior and taxonomy need source review; common name covers multiple species.

item_description: A deep-ocean squid of Antarctic waters, with large eyes and swiveling hooks on its arms and tentacles.
item_facts: It is among the heaviest known squid species.
It lives in the Southern Ocean around Antarctica.
Much of its biology remains difficult to study because it lives at great depths.
needs_review: Size ranking, range and anatomy not externally verified.

item_description: A large herbivorous marine mammal that grazes on seagrass in warm coastal waters of the Indo-Pacific.
item_facts: Dugongs are sirenians, related to manatees.
They depend on seagrass beds for much of their food.
Their range extends from East Africa to the western Pacific.

source_refs.title: Dugongs: biodiversity and seagrass, Dugong & Seagrass Hub

needs_review: Diet and range not externally verified in the source consulted.
Relationship to manatees is not supported by the replacement source and remains for manual review.

item_description: A large octopus of the North Pacific, known for flexible arms, camouflage and problem-solving behavior.
item_facts: It has eight arms lined with suckers.
It can change skin color and texture to blend into its surroundings.
It lives in rocky coastal habitats and feeds on crabs, clams and fish.
needs_review: Species-specific anatomy, behavior and diet not externally verified.

item_description: A deep-sea squid with exceptionally long feeding tentacles and large eyes adapted to low light.
item_facts: It is rarely observed alive because it inhabits the deep ocean.
Its tentacles bear toothed rings or suckers for holding prey.
Sperm whales are known predators of giant squid.
needs_review: Anatomy, observation history and predator claims not externally verified.

item_description: A large predatory shark found in temperate and subtropical seas, with broad triangular teeth and a countershaded body.
item_facts: It occurs in temperate and subtropical waters worldwide.
Its diet can include fish, invertebrates and marine mammals.
It can maintain some body tissues warmer than surrounding water.

item_description: A globally distributed sea turtle whose adults are largely herbivorous and graze on seagrasses and algae.
item_facts: It migrates between feeding grounds and nesting beaches.
Females return to sandy beaches to lay eggs.
Its name comes from the greenish color of its body fat, not its shell.
needs_review: Diet, nesting and name-origin claims not externally verified.

item_description: A migrating baleen whale known for long seasonal journeys, complex songs and cooperative bubble-net feeding in some populations.
item_facts: Humpbacks feed on krill and small schooling fish.
Males produce complex songs that can change over time.
Some groups use bubbles to corral prey before lunging through the school.
needs_review: Feeding and vocalization facts vary across populations; claims not externally verified.

item_description: The largest living turtle, a deep-diving ocean traveler with a flexible, leathery shell.
item_facts: Jellyfish and other soft-bodied animals form a major part of its diet.
It can migrate across entire ocean basins.
Its shell lacks the hard, separate scutes found on most other sea turtles.
needs_review: Size, diet, migration and shell anatomy not externally verified.

item_description: A cold-water jellyfish with a broad bell and long trailing tentacles equipped with stinging cells.
item_facts: It is among the largest known jellyfish by tentacle length.
Its tentacles capture small animals and plankton.
Its coloration can range from pale yellow to deep red or brown.
needs_review: Size ranking, diet and color variation not externally verified.

item_description: A large, wing-shaped ray that swims through tropical and temperate seas while filter-feeding on plankton.
item_facts: Mantas are cartilaginous fish, not mammals.
They use paired cephalic fins beside the mouth to guide water and food inward.
They are generally divided into reef manta and giant manta species.
needs_review: Taxonomy and feeding details need current species-level verification.

item_description: An Arctic toothed whale whose male usually has a long spiral tusk formed from an elongated tooth.
item_facts: Narwhals live in Arctic waters and migrate with seasonal sea ice.
The tusk is an elongated tooth, usually found in males.
Their diet includes Arctic fish, squid and shrimp.

item_description: A highly social, toothed whale found in every ocean, with distinct populations that specialize in different prey.
item_facts: Orcas are the largest members of the dolphin family.
They live in stable social groups called pods.
Different populations can have distinct diets, calls and hunting strategies.
needs_review: Species identity, social structure and population differences not externally verified.

item_description: The largest living crocodilian, found in coastal and freshwater habitats across parts of South and Southeast Asia and Australia.
item_facts: It can travel through seawater between coastal areas.
It is an ambush predator with a varied diet.
Males can defend territories in estuaries and rivers.
needs_review: Size ranking, distribution and behavior not externally verified.

item_description: A marine mammal of the North Pacific that uses dense fur for insulation and often floats at the surface while feeding.
item_facts: It is the smallest marine mammal, though one of the heaviest members of the weasel family.
It uses tools such as rocks to open hard-shelled prey.
By eating sea urchins, it can help maintain kelp forest ecosystems.

source_refs.title: Sea Otter Anatomy, NOAA Ocean Today

needs_review: Size, tool use and ecosystem claims not externally verified.
The size comparison and kelp-ecosystem claim remain unverified.

item_description: A deep-diving toothed whale with the largest brain of any known animal and a distinctive block-shaped head.
item_facts: It uses echolocation to find prey at depth.
Squid are an important part of its diet, including large deep-sea species.
The spermaceti organ in its head is associated with sound production and echolocation.
needs_review: Brain-size claim, diet and organ function not externally verified; avoid presenting historical hypotheses as settled.

item_description: A large Arctic marine mammal with long tusks, whiskers and a thick layer of blubber.
item_facts: Its tusks are elongated canine teeth found in both males and females.
It uses sensitive whiskers to locate clams and other seafloor prey.
Walruses gather on sea ice or coastal haul-outs to rest between feeding trips.
needs_review: Anatomy, feeding and haul-out claims not externally verified.

item_description: The largest fish in the ocean, a filter-feeding shark that consumes plankton and other small organisms.
item_facts: It is a shark, not a whale, and breathes with gills.
Its spot pattern is unique to each individual.
It occurs in tropical and warm-temperate seas around the world.
